facts.fact_text: A demonstration was held at Slavyanskaya Square as part of the 'Right March'.
The 'Right March' attracted several thousand people, according to the applicants.
Despite the position of the district authority, the organisers decided to hold a public gathering in Tverskaya Square on 27 November 2005 at 2 p.m.
On 23 November 2005 the Moscow city administration stated that it would give permission only for the demonstration, not the march.
The Moscow city administration wanted the demonstration to be held in Tverskaya Zastava Square instead of Tverskaya Square.
The Moscow city administration wanted the demonstration to last one hour instead of two hours.
In a letter of 24 November 2005, the district authority suggested that the picket event be held in Tverskaya Zastava Square instead of Tverskaya Square.
In its letter of 24 November 2005, the district authority suggested the picket event run from 2 p.m. to 3 p.m. instead of 2 p.m. to 4 p.m.
The special security squad proceeded to arrest some participants at the public gathering in Tverskaya Square on 27 November 2005.

Under sections 5 and 7 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act in force at the relevant time, the organiser of a public event (except for an event involving one person) was required to inform the competent authority of the event at least ten days in advance.

Under sections 5 and 7 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act in force at the relevant time, the organiser of a picket (пикетирование) was required to inform the competent authority at least three days in advance.

Under sections 5 and 7 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, the organiser was required to indicate the purpose of the event, its form, the venue and the itinerary, as well as the date, timing and approximate number of participants.
Under the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, the competent authority was required to notify the organiser if it had a reasoned proposal for another venue and/or timing for the event.
Under the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, the organiser was required to inform the competent authority whether he or she refused or accepted the suggested new venue and/or timing.
Under section 5 § 5 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, the event could not take place if the event organiser and the competent authority had not approved the alternative proposal.
Under section 16 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, a public event could be stopped if there was a real threat to life or physical integrity of persons or property.
Under section 16 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, a public event could be stopped if the event participants had acted unlawfully.

Under section 16 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, a public event could be stopped if the event organiser had knowingly breached the requirements of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act as regards the conduct of the event.

Under section 17 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, the representative of the public authority present at the event could order the event organiser to put an end to the event in circumstances justifying stoppage.
Under section 17 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, the public authority representative was required to explain the reasons for the order to stop the event and provide time for compliance.
Under section 17 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, if the organiser had not complied with the order to stop the event, the public official could issue the same order to the participants.

Under section 17 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, if both the organiser and participants failed to comply with the order to stop the event, the police was to take appropriate measures to stop the event.

Under section 8 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, a public event could not be held in zones close to dangerous industrial objects, the residences of the President of the Russian Federation, court buildings or prisons.
Under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, a violation of the procedure concerning a public gathering is punishable by a fine.
The district authority's letter of 24 November 2005 referred to the need to avoid causing obstruction to pedestrians and vehicles as a reason for the suggested change of venue and timing.
The district authority explained in its letter of 24 November 2005 that under a 1998 order the area around the Dolgorukiy monument was restricted to service vehicles of the Moscow mayor's office.
Under section 16 of the 2004 Public Gatherings Act, a public event could be stopped if there was a real threat to life or physical integrity of persons or property.
The Moscow city administration wanted the demonstration to be held in Tverskaya Zastava Square instead of Tverskaya Square.
The Moscow city administration wanted the demonstration to last one hour instead of two hours.
In a letter of 24 November 2005, the district authority suggested that the picket event be held in Tverskaya Zastava Square instead of Tverskaya Square.
In its letter of 24 November 2005, the district authority suggested the picket event run from 2 p.m. to 3 p.m. instead of 2 p.m. to 4 p.m.
The Justice of the Peace referred to the district authority's letter of 24 November 2005 in concluding that the public gathering was unlawful.
